3. A supplementary affidavit has also been filed by the applicant in support of the application for re-hearing annexing the certified copy of the judgment passed on 26-11-2001 in the Civil revision, the photostat copy of the certified copy of the judgment and decree dated 8th August, 1994 passed in Title Appeal No. 74 of 1991 and the photostat copy of the affidavit sworn by Md Habibur Rahman Mollah and Mosammat Rahima Khatun. In the supplementary affidavit it has been stated that the instant Civil revision was filed against the judgment and decree dated 28-11-93 passed in Title Appeal No. 62 of 1991 by the learned Additional District Judge, Madaripur who mostly relied upon the application filed by said Mosammat Rahima Khatun and the evidence of Md Habibur Rahman Mollah. Said Rahima Khatun was not examined in Court for which she could not be cross- examined in Title Suit No. 54 of 1986. But subsequently truth revealed when Rahima Khatun and Md Habibur Rahman Mollah had sworn an affidavit on 30-4-2002, signature of said Rahirna Khatun was also fraudulently obtained to file that application. Three suits were filed by Meherunnesa against her sons, daughters and grandsons. In all the three suits the main and substantial question was as to whether the concerned deed of gift was genuine or created fraudulently on obtaining the thumb impression of Meherunnesa who was suffering from old age diseases. From the 3(three) suits three title Appeals arose. The trial Court and the appellate Court passed 6 judgments while in 5 judgments the Court below decided the question in favour of the plaintiff and held that the respective deed of gift was not genuine and possession of the lands transferred by the deeds was not handed over. Only in Title Appeal No. 62 of 1991 the appellate Court relying on the application of Rahim Khatun, held that the deed of gift was genuine and further held that there was defect of parties in the suit. The appellate Court also failed to consider that Rahima Khatun was not reliable as she also claimed some quantum of land by virtue of a deed of gift and the alleged defect of parties was not fatal in the suit in view of the provision of rule 9 of Order I of the Code of Civil Procedure, particularly when there was no dispute with regard to the title of the plaintiff (Meherunnessa). Further, the Appellate Court did not say anything about the possession of the parties in the suit land, whereas, the question of possession was a vital point for giving effect to a deed of gift in Muslim Law. The finding of the trial Court to the effect "the heirs of the plaintiff Meherunnesa have been possessing the suit land and the defendants are not in possession" have not been reversed by the appellate Court and, as such, the Rule in Civil Revision No. 2581 of 1991 ought to have been made absolute by this Court. Out of high anxiety the applicant filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1493 of 2002 before the Appellate Division only to save limitation from the date of knowledge and the same may be withdrawn if this Court allows this application for re-hearing. 

 7. It appears that this application for re-hearing was filed on 22-4-2002, whereas, leave petition was filed on 16-9-2002. In the supplementary affidavit it has been categorically stated that out of 'high anxiety' leave petition was filed only to save limitation. I do not see any legal bar in disposing of this application on merit as mere filing of a leave petition does not ipso facto take away the jurisdiction of this Court, unless any interim order was passed by the Appellate Division regulating the proceeding of the High Court Division. Therefore, I proceed to dispose of the application on merit.
